title: Icing: Where It Lives, How You Leave

faa.title: Pilot Guide: Flight in Icing Conditions

hook: Ice doesn't announce itself. It just starts redesigning your wing.

scenes.narration: Thirty seconds. Airframe icing — the only passenger that boards mid-flight and never pays.
The recipe: visible moisture plus a surface at or below freezing. Zero to minus twenty — that's the kitchen.
Clear ice: big drops, smooth, heavy — the sneaky one. Rime: instant, white, brittle. Mixed: both, because the sky likes variety.
Before you file: where's the freezing level, the warm air, the clear air? Freezing rain means warm air is ABOVE you.
onScreenText: Freezing level · warm air · clear air
Freezing rain → warm air is above

scenes.narration: The best de-ice equipment is the altitude where it isn't. File with an out.
A C ninety-one dash seventy-four bravo. Stay warm.

quiz.question: Structural icing requires:
choices: Visible moisture and aircraft surface temperature at or below freezing
quiz.explanation: Both ingredients are required: visible moisture (cloud, rain) and a surface at or below 0°C. (AC 91-74B)

quiz.question: Which icing type comes from large supercooled drops and forms smooth, heavy, hard-to-see accretions?
quiz.explanation: Clear ice flows back before freezing, building smooth heavy sheets — the most dangerous accretion type.

quiz.question: You encounter freezing rain. The warmer air you may need is most likely:
quiz.explanation: Freezing rain forms when precipitation falls from warmer air aloft into a below-freezing layer — a climb may reach the warm layer.
